question: How does uncertainty in the observation process change which BAM ecological worlds can be exactly falsified by the same survey history?

finite_world_construction.target_node_rule: Among landscape nodes, choose the lexicographically first node maximizing min(number of ecological worlds with target in G, number with target outside G).
finite_world_construction.ecological_truth_rule: Choose the lexicographically first ecological world with target absent, focal source retained, and at least two occupied nodes.

calibration_evidence.effect: retain only joint worlds whose observation-world p equals the calibrated value
calibration_evidence.boundary: This is an identifiability upper-bound calibration channel, not a claim that p is known exactly in field surveys.

hypotheses.claim: A joint world is compatible exactly when the observed detection history has positive probability under the observation process conditional on the ecological world's target state.
hypotheses.rule: Any mismatch between direct probability calculation and joint compatibility refutes J1.

hypotheses.claim: For the frozen all-zero history, broadening the observation universe from perfect detection to include p=0.75 strictly increases the ecological-world projection by retaining target-present worlds that perfect detection excludes.
hypotheses.rule: Failure of strict subset expansion refutes J2.

hypotheses.claim: Starting from the broad joint universe, direct calibration to p=1 removes the imperfect-detection joint worlds and restores exactly the same ecological-world projection as the strict universe, without collecting a new focal ecological observation.
hypotheses.rule: Any projection mismatch between calibrated-broad and strict refutes J3.

hypotheses.claim: With p=0.75 retained as admissible, finite all-zero histories at n=1,2,4,8 all leave at least one target-present ecological world compatible.
hypotheses.rule: Any finite n in the frozen set eliminating every target-present ecological world under the broad universe refutes J4.

hypotheses.claim: Expanding the admissible observation-world set cannot remove an ecological world from the projected compatible set.
hypotheses.rule: Any ecological survivor under a narrower observation universe that disappears after expansion refutes J5.

hypotheses.claim: In the frozen case, four additional nondetections (n=8 total) do not shrink the broad ecological projection to the strict projection, whereas p=1 calibration does.
hypotheses.rule: If n=8 broad projection equals strict, or calibrated projection does not equal strict, J6 is refuted.

claim_boundary: Ecological falsification is robust only after quantifying over the declared observation-world universe.
A world excluded under one observation model may become compatible when observation uncertainty is expanded.
Calibration can change the interpretation of already-collected observations without changing ecological truth.
The result remains conditional on finite ecological and observation world universes.
